paragraphs.title: The Command and Warning to the Priests

easy.explanation: The verse says, “O ye priests, this commandment is for you.”
easy.q: To whom is the commandment addressed at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: The LORD commands them to “give glory unto my name.”
easy.q: What were the priests required to give unto God's name?

easy.explanation: The LORD warns, “I will even send a curse upon you.”
easy.q: What would the LORD send if the priests would not hear?

medium.explanation: The LORD says, “I will curse your blessings.”
medium.q: What would happen to the priests' blessings if they would not lay the commandment to heart?

medium.explanation: The curse is a punishment threatened because of disobedience.
medium.q: What does the word “curse” mean in this passage?

answers: It required obedience and honor toward God's name
It was intended only for gaining wealth
medium.explanation: The priests were required to hear God's command and honor His name.
medium.q: What does the warning show about the priests' sacred service?

answers: The priests were persistently ignoring the command
The priests had already corrected their ways
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that they were not taking the command seriously.
challenge.q: What does the repeated phrase “lay it to heart” emphasize?

answers: Disregard for God's name would bring a curse upon the blessings
Honoring God's name would remove every blessing
challenge.explanation: The LORD connects failure to honor His name with the cursing of their blessings.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between honoring God's name and the priests' blessings?

answers: That God's covenant might be with Levi
That the priests might become kings
That the covenant might be abolished
challenge.explanation: The LORD says the commandment was sent “that my covenant might be with Levi.”
challenge.q: What was the purpose of sending this commandment to the priests?

paragraphs.title: The Proper Model of the House of Levi

easy.explanation: The covenant is described as “my covenant ... of life and peace.”
easy.q: What did the LORD give to Levi through the covenant?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The law of truth was in his mouth.”
easy.q: What was in the priest's mouth according to the passage?

easy.explanation: The priests' lips were to keep knowledge, and the people were to seek the law at his mouth.
easy.q: What did the people seek at the priest's mouth?

medium.explanation: The LORD says He gave Levi the covenant because Levi feared Him.
medium.q: What effect did fear of the LORD have upon Levi?

answers: His words were free from wickedness
medium.explanation: The statement describes the truth and integrity of Levi's teaching.
medium.q: What does “iniquity was not found in his lips” mean in context?

answers: He turned many away from iniquity
medium.explanation: The verse says Levi “did turn many away from iniquity.”
medium.q: What was the result of Levi's walking with God in peace and equity?

answers: Because the people were to seek the law at his mouth
Because the priest was required to be wealthy
Because the priest had no responsibility toward the people
challenge.explanation: The people depended on the priest to preserve and teach God's law.
challenge.q: Why was the law of truth essential to the priest's calling?

answers: Fear of God, truth, integrity, and turning people from sin
Silence, isolation, and withdrawal from the people
challenge.explanation: These qualities and actions are presented in the description of Levi.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the proper model of Levi?

answers: The priest was to communicate God's law to the people
The priest was a military king
The priest did not need to teach
challenge.explanation: The title follows the description of the priest's duty to preserve knowledge and teach the law.
challenge.q: What does “he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts” mean in this context?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “ye are departed out of the way.”
easy.q: From what had the priests departed?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “ye have caused many to stumble at the law.”
easy.q: Whom had the priests caused to stumble?

easy.explanation: The LORD says He made them “contemptible and base before all the people.”
easy.q: How did the priests become before all the people?

answers: They did not keep God's ways and were partial in the law
medium.explanation: Their humiliation resulted from failing to keep God's ways and showing partiality.
medium.q: Why did the priests become contemptible and base?

answers: Showing favoritism instead of judging fairly
Carrying a scroll of the law
medium.explanation: The phrase describes biased and unequal treatment in judgment.
medium.q: What does “partial in the law” mean in this passage?

answers: The priests' wrong path led others into error
Their departure caused many to learn truth
medium.explanation: Their own departure from God's way resulted in others stumbling at the law.
medium.q: What connection is made between departing from the way and causing many to stumble?

answers: Their calling and the people's trust in them
challenge.explanation: Corrupting the covenant harmed both their priestly responsibility and their standing before the people.
challenge.q: What was damaged when the priests corrupted the covenant of Levi?

answers: They were responsible for keeping and teaching God's law
They had no connection with the law
They were responsible only for building the temple
challenge.explanation: Their calling required them to preserve knowledge and teach the law faithfully.
challenge.q: Why was being partial in the law especially serious for the priests?

answers: Levi walked in integrity, but the priests departed from the way
Levi was partial, but the priests taught truth
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts Levi's faithful example with the priests' corruption.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between Levi's example and the priests' failure?

paragraphs.title: Betrayal of the Ancestors' Covenant and Foreign Marriages

easy.explanation: The verse asks, “Have we not all one father? hath not one God created us?”
easy.q: How many fathers and how many Gods are mentioned as the basis of unity?

easy.explanation: The passage asks why they dealt treacherously “every man against his brother.”
easy.q: Against whom did Judah deal treacherously?

answers: The daughter of a strange god
easy.explanation: The verse says he “hath married the daughter of a strange god.”
easy.q: Whom did the man marry in the passage?

answers: All the people shared one father and one God
The people had no connection with one another
medium.explanation: Their shared origin and worship created a covenant responsibility toward one another.
medium.q: Why is dealing treacherously with one's brother connected with profaning the covenant?

answers: A woman associated with the worship of another god
The daughter of an Israelite priest
The wife of the man's youth
medium.explanation: The phrase identifies a woman connected with a foreign god.
medium.q: What does “the daughter of a strange god” mean in context?

answers: The holiness of the LORD and the covenant of the fathers
medium.explanation: Judah is said to have profaned the holiness of the LORD through this unfaithfulness.
medium.q: What was profaned by the marriage described in the passage?

answers: Shared faith requires people not to betray their brothers
Faith has no connection with human relationships
challenge.explanation: The question about one father and one God is immediately followed by a rebuke for betraying one's brother.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between belief in one God and responsibility toward other people?

answers: It profaned the LORD's holiness and violated the fathers' covenant
challenge.explanation: The act is treated as a violation of God's holiness and the covenant community.
challenge.q: Why is marrying the daughter of a strange god presented as more than a private matter?

answers: One father and God, betrayal of a brother, and profaning the covenant
The temple, sacrifice, and a feast
challenge.explanation: These ideas appear in that order in the passage.
challenge.q: What is the main progression of thought in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Wives' Tears and Violation of the Marriage Covenant

easy.explanation: The verse describes the altar as covered with “tears, with weeping, and with crying out.”
easy.q: What covered the altar of the LORD?

answers: The daughter of a strange god
easy.explanation: She is called “the wife of thy youth” and “the wife of thy covenant.”
easy.q: Who was the woman against whom the man dealt treacherously?

easy.explanation: The passage repeatedly commands, “take heed to your spirit.”
easy.q: What were the people commanded to take heed to?

answers: The offering was not received with good will
medium.explanation: The LORD says He regarded not the offering and did not receive it with good will.
medium.q: What was the result of the tears and cries at the altar?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to receiving the offering from the people who brought it.
medium.q: What does the phrase “at your hand” mean in “receiveth it with good will at your hand”?

answers: It is a binding relationship between husband and wife
It is only a temporary arrangement
medium.explanation: The wife is described as the man's companion and the wife of his covenant.
medium.q: Why is marriage called a covenant in this passage?

answers: The betrayal causes the offering to be rejected
The betrayal makes the offering more acceptable
challenge.explanation: The tears caused by the betrayal are directly connected with the LORD's refusal to accept the offering favorably.
challenge.q: What connection is made between wronging the wife and worship at the altar?

answers: Inner self-control is needed to prevent treachery
Only an outward ceremony is required
Feelings and intentions do not matter
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes inward responsibility, restraint, and faithfulness.
challenge.q: What does the repeated command to take heed to one's spirit suggest?

answers: The first is presented as a covenant companion, while the second is foreign to the covenant
Both are presented in exactly the same role
The wife of one's youth is foreign, while the other is the covenant companion
challenge.explanation: The passage honors faithfulness to the wife of one's covenant and condemns turning to a foreign relationship.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the wife of one's youth and the daughter of a strange god?

paragraphs.title: Questioning God's Justice and Distorted Morality

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Ye have wearied the LORD with your words.”
easy.q: With what had the people wearied the LORD?

answers: He is good in the sight of the LORD
easy.explanation: They said, “Every one that doeth evil is good in the sight of the LORD.”
easy.q: What did they say about the person who does evil?

answers: Where is the God of judgment?
Where is the king of Israel?
easy.explanation: The verse ends with the question, “Where is the God of judgment?”
easy.q: What question did they ask about God?

answers: Both challenge the way God's justice is understood
Both concern the building of the altar
medium.explanation: The people call evildoers good and then question where God's judgment is.
medium.q: What connection exists between the two claims in the verse?

medium.explanation: The LORD describes their words as causing Him weariness.
medium.q: What does “wearied” mean in this context?

answers: They blurred the distinction between good and evil
They clearly distinguished good from evil
They refused to ask any question about justice
medium.explanation: They called those who did evil good in the sight of the LORD.
medium.q: What moral view is revealed by the people's words?

answers: It follows their claim that evildoers are good in God's sight
It follows praise for righteous deeds
It has no connection with their earlier statement
challenge.explanation: The context shows that they were questioning whether God judged rightly.
challenge.q: Why does the question “Where is the God of judgment?” express doubt rather than a simple request for information?

challenge.explanation: The verse quotes them as saying that the person who does evil is good in the LORD's sight.
challenge.q: What is the central verbal distortion in the people's statement?

answers: Both expose corruption in the proper order of worship, teaching, and judgment
challenge.explanation: Earlier passages expose corrupt priestly service, while this verse exposes distorted ideas about justice.
challenge.q: How does this passage connect with the earlier rebukes in the chapter?
